registrationNote: New registration, not an edit. v1.0.0 (c977347), v1.1.0 (1a8256f) and v1.2.0 (7e9e55f + Amendments 1-2) are preserved byte-for-byte, each governing its own results. v1.3.0 exists to pay the single committed gate recorded at the program's close (STATUS committedGates: v1.3.0-I12-decision-enforcement, owner direction at RUN-20260807-3's close, evidence doubled at RUN-20260807-4): it registers I12, the invariant that makes the program's two owner decisions checkable instead of fixture-pinned. The program was closed at RUN-20260807-4 and is deliberately reopened for this gate only (RUN-20260807-5). The evaluator under test is bit-identical to v1.0.0's. This is an enforcement change, not a semantics change: every count, every conclusion, and both pinned digests must be unchanged.
question: Do the registered owner decisions (R1 tie rule, R5.2 absolute margin) have an invariant with power against their inversion -- and does adding that invariant change nothing about what the evaluator does?
null: I12 catches the R1-inverting ablation on other than exactly 22,440 exhaustive worlds, or the R5.2-inverting ablation on other than exactly 38,760, or B5 records any I12 violation, or any registered value moves.
target: I12 catches the two inversions at exactly the registered counts with no fixture involved; B5 records zero I12 violations; every value in expectedIdenticalToRun1 including both pinned digests reproduced exactly.

repairs.title: I12: decision enforcement
repairs.resolves: SPEC-110/SPEC-112 (findings G4/H2): both owner decisions were enforced by zero invariants; an evaluator inverting either passed all eleven invariants over the complete enumeration and was caught only by pinned fixtures (R1: C11+C12; R5.2: C12 alone).
repairs.statement: See invariants[11] (I12). Hard invariant: for every receipt-producing world, conclusion equals conclusionFunction(world) computed from the WORLD (not the receipt), and margin equals abs(count of distinct supporting roots - count of distinct opposing roots), likewise from the world. Subsumes I2's and I5's conclusion clauses (their registered statements are carried verbatim; their receipt-internal defect F1/F2 remains open and separate).
repairs.decidedBy: owner (committed gate, RUN-20260807-3 close; executed on owner direction, RUN-20260807-5)
repairs.ownerDecisionNote: The gate itself was an owner decision; I12's content is a derivation from the registered conclusionFunction and R5.2 -- there is nothing here that could defensibly have gone another way, which is what distinguishes it from R1/R5.2.
repairs.subDecisionsNote: Stated per the G5 lesson. (1) I12 emits AT MOST ONE violation per world, its detail naming whether conclusion, margin, or both diverged -- so caught-counts equal world counts and the registered 22,440/38,760 are exact-match targets. (2) The decision-ablation phase contains no fixture comparison of any kind; the catch is the checker's alone, which is what the registered 'no fixture involved' requires. (3) Baseline continuity: B1-B4's registered totals are sums over I1-I11 and are preserved unchanged as the registered power metric; their I12 counts are reported SEPARATELY as i12Violations (new information beside the preserved metric -- folding them in would move every baseline total, since all four baselines' conclusion distributions differ from the reference's). I12's power is established by the two dedicated ablations at exact registered counts, not by B1-B4. (4) I12 is skipped where no receipt exists (fail-closed and inadmissible worlds), like every receipt-referential check.
repairs.expectedNumericChange: none anywhere except the two new ablation measurements and the new reported-only i12Violations figures
repairs.verifiedExistingBehaviour: B5's conformance to I12 is exactly what IND-20260807-2/-3 established (identical conclusion distribution) and what RUN-3/RUN-4's reference-side ablations measured from the other direction; the 22,440 and 38,760 counts are prior measurements from both implementations, registered here as pass conditions rather than predictions

decisionAblations.note: The positive controls for I12, replacing fixture-coincidence with registered measurement. Each ablation is B5 with ONE owner decision inverted and nothing else, run over the complete exhaustive enumeration through the same checker that clears B5. No fixture is consulted anywhere in this phase.

ablations.description: ties and strict minorities on presence claims conclude supported (the IND-20260807-1 existential reading)
margin is signed: count(supporting) - count(opposing) (the IND-20260807-1/-2 reading)

decisionAblations.invalidation: A caught-count differing from the registered value in either direction invalidates the run and is the primary finding: I12 is then wrong, not the measurement. Any non-I12 violation by an ablation is likewise a finding (prior measurements recorded zero).

baselineReporting.preservedMetric: totalViolations = sum over I1-I11, byte-comparable to every prior version; MUST equal the registered values (B1 634440, B2 26880, B3 26208, B4 189720).
baselineReporting.newInformation: i12Violations reported per baseline, separately. Not registered as an expected value (never previously measured; registering a prediction would require pre-execution). Expected to be strictly positive for every baseline whose conclusion distribution differs from the reference's, which is all four; reported for information and for future registration.

conclusionFunction.admissibility: Input must parse and be well-formed (I9); the declared search space must be non-empty (R2); location ids must be pairwise distinct (I11); every evidence side must be 'support' or 'oppose'; no rootId may appear on both sides (I3). Inadmissible input refuses fail-closed: no receipt exists.
conclusionFunction.presence: supported iff |distinct supporting roots| > |distinct opposing roots|, else not_established. Ties are not_established (R1, owner decision, v1.1.0).
conclusionFunction.absence: present if any distinct opposing root exists (I5); else absent_within_declared_scope if search.complete (which requires every declared location searched and declared > 0); else not_established.
conclusionFunction.note: Carried verbatim from v1.1.0/v1.2.0. NEW IN v1.3.0: this function is enforced by I12 rather than being prose with fixtures behind it. The A1 and A2 readings embedded in this text (absence gates on coverage alone; presence has no coverage term) remain UNDECIDED owner decisions recorded in STATUS permanentLimits -- I12 enforces the registered text as written without deciding them, and a future decision on either would be a new registration whose surface (4 and 19,152 worlds) is already measured.

invariants.name: copy invariance
invariants.statement: Appending a duplicate of any existing record (same rootId, same side) leaves conclusion, distinctRoots, supportingRoots, opposingRoots, margin, and conversionsToReverse unchanged, and increases records and repeatedRecordsCollapsed by exactly 1 each.

invariants.name: bounded absence
invariants.statement: conclusion == 'absent_within_declared_scope' implies search.complete is true and opposingRoots is empty. Equivalently no absence conclusion is reachable while any location status is not 'searched'.
invariants.carryNote: Verbatim from v1.0.0 including the known-defective 'Equivalently' (F1, open). Its conclusion clause is now subsumed by I12.

invariants.name: side separation
invariants.statement: If any rootId appears with both sides, evaluation raises and no receipt is produced.

invariants.name: deterministic replay
invariants.statement: Evaluating the same world twice yields byte-identical canonical JSON and an equal contentDigest, per canonicalForm and receiptObject.

invariants.name: counterexample dominance
invariants.statement: For absence claims, a non-empty opposingRoots implies conclusion == 'present', at any coverage level.
invariants.carryNote: Verbatim; receipt-internal defect F2 open; conclusion clause now subsumed by I12.

invariants.name: digest integrity
invariants.statement: verify_content_digest holds for every emitted receipt, and fails for every single-field mutation of one.

invariants.name: order invariance
invariants.statement: Permuting locations or records changes no evidential field, no conclusion, and no contentDigest.

invariants.name: search arithmetic
invariants.statement: declared == len(locations), searched and unavailable equal their status counts, searched + unavailable <= declared, and complete == (searched == declared and declared > 0).

invariants.name: fail-closed parsing
invariants.statement: Malformed input raises an exception and never returns a receipt.
invariants.coverageNote: Still exercised by zero non-adversarial worlds (reinstated ledger item).

invariants.name: copies never mint roots
invariants.statement: distinctRoots equals the number of distinct rootId values in the input, and appending any number of copies of existing roots leaves it unchanged.

invariants.name: location identifier uniqueness
invariants.statement: The id values of searchLedger.locations must be pairwise distinct; duplicates refuse fail-closed with no receipt.

invariants.name: decision enforcement
invariants.statement: For every receipt-producing world: conclusion equals conclusionFunction(world), computed from the world's evidence and search ledgers rather than from any receipt field; and margin equals abs(count of distinct supporting roots - count of distinct opposing roots), likewise computed from the world. At most one I12 violation is emitted per world; its detail states which of the two equalities failed, or both. Skipped where no receipt exists.
invariants.v130Note: New. This is the committed gate: the invariant with power against the inversion of either owner decision (R1, R5.2). Registered pass condition: catches ABL-R1 on exactly 22,440 worlds and ABL-R52 on exactly 38,760, with no fixture involved; B5 records zero.

successCondition: Zero hard-invariant violations by B5 across all twelve invariants and all phases; ABL-R1 caught by I12 on exactly 22,440 worlds and ABL-R52 on exactly 38,760, each with zero other-invariant violations and no fixture involved; baselines' preserved totals unchanged and non-zero; C11/C12 digests unchanged; every value in expectedIdenticalToRun1 equal to observation.
failureCondition: Any hard-invariant violation by B5, including any I12 violation.
invalidationCondition: Any prior-version invalidation condition; any expectedIdenticalToRun1 value differing from observation; either ablation caught at a count other than its registered value (in either direction -- I12 is then wrong, not the measurement; stop and report rather than adjust); any non-I12 violation by an ablation.
stopCondition: One hard violation halts and preserves the world. One moved value or one wrong ablation count halts the run with that as the primary finding.

claimDiscipline.strongestSupportedIfPassed: Within the declared bounds, the reference evaluator conforms to protocol v1.3.0; the two owner decisions are enforced by invariant I12, whose power against each decision's inversion is demonstrated at the exact previously measured surface (22,440 and 38,760 worlds) with no fixture involved; and the enforcement change altered nothing the evaluator does -- no count, conclusion, or pinned digest moved.
claimDiscipline.establishedAlready: Cross-implementation conformance per KL-000/FINAL-RECORD.md: evaluator and conclusion function across the full enumeration; canonical form and digests for the two pinned receipts; qualified by LEAK-101; both implementations at zero violations in every run.
claimDiscipline.notEstablished: That the independent implementation conforms to v1.3.0 (it has not run against it; its checker choices are its own). 'Verified' in any form. A1/A2 (undecided, 4 and 19,152 worlds). The randomized phase across implementations. Anything outside the declared bounds. Any part of a knowledge transaction, cross-system result, or First Transmission -- the first-transaction gate is NOT REACHED.
claimDiscipline.ifFailed: A wrong ablation count is the primary finding (I12 wrong, not the measurement). A moved value is worse (enforcement changed semantics). Either halts the run and is reported, never adjusted.
